commenti.body:
Yes, it's a very thoughtful movie even if the main metaphor -- becoming an internet meme -- is so obvious that the movie quickly merges the metaphor with the direct meaning. It's admirable that it was not all wrapped up nicely in some fake Hollywood ending.

I highly recommend the director's previous movie, Sick of Myself, which is a devastating takedown of social media as a performative mental/physical illness. He's the best satirist of online culture in movies today.

Spoilers:

Watching this film I had an experience I’ve come to dread when watching a film, that of the narrative drastically changing and the tone that’s been built up being obliterated in a single scene. 

It does seem hard to wrap up high concept films in a satisfying manner, to have a third act that deepens the experience and brings it all to a close, and maybe I’m spoiled by all the amazing Charlie Kaufman scripts we’ve gotten over his lifetime, but when Dream Scenario cut to the infomercial for the device, and the influencer advertisement angle, I was immediately out on the whole film.

The main conceit of the film is so bananas in the first place, and I don’t think it needed explanation or anything to satisfy the film as a whole, but now a device can do the same thing? and this is how it’s used? The satire of it felt sudden and forced, and although I enjoyed cage’s performance it soured the entire movie for me
It’s Walmart brand Kaufman, it has many of his signature elements with the affable male protagonist and surrealism but none of the depth or emotion that makes his scripts great.

In anticipation of this movie I watched the filmmaker’s other one, Sick of Myself, which is more focused and a better film (still not great) but suffers the same fate as the satire takes a stranglehold over the plot and characters

I left unsatisfied. I felt this film lost its narrative direction. There were ideas that felt under developed. It took sharp turns that lacked cohesion. I wanted something more developed, not necessarily neat and tidy or fully explained, but with tighter writing and more fully explored concepts. There were weird sci-fi like aspects, a little drama and emotion, humor, some horror, cultural commentary, but not enough of any of it to make it work for me. Fewer ideas more fully developed. I enjoyed Cage performance, and i sensed he could have had more script to work with so that too felt thin. The sex-gone-bad scene was hilarious.

I loved *Dream Scenario* and will come back to engage with this review, but thank you for the top-line mention of *The Boy and the Heron.* It’s playing near me, and I debated going this weekend.

But while I am open-minded about animation’s potential for filmmaking and appreciative of Miyazaki, I think I needed to see that note from someone in my shoes to get me off the fence.
I found that his relationship with his wife offered a lot of depth and emotion. If they hadn’t included that he would have been completely unlikeable.

Spoilers:

I loved the first half of this film - especially the “twist” where Cage’s character goes from internet darling one night to ostracized and reviled the next - I could definitely see the through lines to modern society. 

There are many times where I love the plot and world building of a film and think to myself while watching, “Please land the plane” as in please don’t ruin this awesome concept with a botched ending or conclusion. It’s easy to get the plane in the air, to have a great idea and demonstrate it on screen, but to give that idea, the plot, and the characters a satisfying ending is where so many promising films falter. 

Dream Scenario is one of those films. It did not land the plane. I found myself completely baffled by the pivot to influencers and it was here I felt the movie ran out of gas and ultimately collapsed under the lofty weight of the first two acts. 

Would recommend Paprika as a film that pairs well with this one if you’re interested!
